s0101.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he was replaced and summoned back; Boli thereupon delayed and would not depart.
s0101.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year he was relieved and summoned home, but Boli delayed and would not set out.

s0102.literal: That year, in the tenth month, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Censor-in-Chief Xu Junfu memorialized, saying: "Your servant has heard that one does not await the carriage and boots—this is the general rule for a lord's command; to rise early and never slacken is the constant duty of a minister.
s0102.idiomatic: That year, in the tenth month, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and censor-in-chief Xu Junfu memorialized: "I have heard that one does not await carriage and boots—such is the rule of a lord's command; rising early and never slackening is a minister's constant duty.

s0103.literal: I respectfully report on Cloud-Banner General, Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Wuxing Military Affairs and Administrator of Wuxing, the Prince of Wuling, Boli: from early on he excelled in fine plans, long bore an excellent reputation, was entrusted as the worthy man, and his native district was his charge.
s0103.idiomatic: I respectfully report on cloud-banner general, bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Wuxing military affairs and administrator of Wuxing, Prince of Wuling Boli: from early on he excelled in counsel and long bore a fine reputation; the realm entrusted him and his native district was his charge.

s0104.literal: His Majesty cherishes and nurtures the black-haired people and keeps his mind on the root of government, seeking together to relieve suffering and soon meeting the imperial heart—yet he again was slow in returning his carriage-team, shifting the season of warmth, delaying his homeward sails, vainly lingering on the road. Gentle caution was not shown; disobedience and sloth were present. To bind faults and examine traces is fitting as a warning.
s0104.idiomatic: His Majesty cherishes the people and keeps his mind on government, seeking together to relieve suffering as the throne wished—yet he again delayed his return, shifting the season's warmth, lingering on the road with homeward sails belated. Gentle caution went unshown; sloth and disobedience stood plain. Faults must be bound and traces examined as a warning.

s0105.literal: We your servants jointly propose that, on the present case, Boli be removed from the offices he holds, that he return to his princely residence, and we respectfully submit this white memorandum for report.
s0105.idiomatic: We jointly propose that on the present case Boli be removed from office, sent back to his residence, and we respectfully submit this report.

s0107.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the Pass; in the Daye era of Sui he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Administrator of Lintao.
s0107.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the Pass; under Sui's Daye era he served as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and administrator of Lintao.

s0108.literal: The Prince of Yongyang, Bozhi, styled Ce Zhi, was Emperor Wen's twelfth son.
s0108.idiomatic: Prince Bozhi of Yongyang, styled Ce Zhi, was Emperor Wen's twelfth son.

s0109.literal: In youth he was steady and generous, had capacity and judgment, and read widely in the classics and histories.
s0109.idiomatic: In youth he was steady and generous, with sound judgment, and read widely in the classics and histories.

s0110.literal: In the Taijian era he was established as Prince of Yongyang.
s0110.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he was made Prince of Yongyang.

s0111.literal: Soon he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Brightly Martial General, with staff clerks appointed.
s0111.idiomatic: Soon he was made attendant-in-ordinary and brightly martial general, with staff clerks appointed.

s0112.literal: Soon he was additionally Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and by successive promotions reached Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Dongyang and Feng Military Affairs, and Pacifying-East General, concurrently holding the post of Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
s0112.idiomatic: Soon he was also regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and rose through posts to left vice director of the masters of writing; he went out as bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Dongyang and Feng military affairs, and pacifying-east general, concurrently interior minister of Kuaiji.

s0113.literal: In the second year of Zhide he entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Assistant General, with special advancement.
s0113.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 he entered court as attendant-in-ordinary and left assistant general, with special advancement.

s0114.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the Pass.
s0114.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the Pass.

s0115.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was made Vice Governor of Qi Prefecture, then promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
s0115.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was vice governor of Qi prefecture, then promoted to vice director of the directorate of education.

s0116.literal: The Prince of Guiyang, Bomou, styled Shen Zhi, was Emperor Wen's thirteenth son.
s0116.idiomatic: Prince Bomou of Guiyang, styled Shen Zhi, was Emperor Wen's thirteenth son.

s0117.literal: In the Taijian era he was established as Prince of Guiyang.
s0117.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he was made Prince of Guiyang.

s0118.literal: In the seventh year he was made Brightly Martial General, with staff clerks appointed.
s0118.idiomatic: In year 7 he was made brightly martial general, with staff clerks appointed.

s0119.literal: Soon he was made Trustworthy Martial General and Governor of Danyang.
s0119.idiomatic: Soon he was made trustworthy martial general and governor of Danyang.

s0120.literal: In the tenth year he was additionally Attendant-in-Ordinary.
s0120.idiomatic: In year 10 he was additionally attendant-in-ordinary.

s0121.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Wuxing Military Affairs, Eastern Central Commander-in-Chief, and Administrator of Wuxing.
s0121.idiomatic: He went out as bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Wuxing military affairs, eastern central commander-in-chief, and administrator of Wuxing.

s0122.literal: In the eleventh year he was additionally Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
s0122.idiomatic: In year 11 he was additionally regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

s0123.literal: In the first year of Zhide he died.

s0124.literal: His son Feng succeeded; in the Daye era he was made Magistrate of Fanhe.
s0124.idiomatic: His son Feng succeeded; under the Daye era he was magistrate of Fanhe.

s0125.literal: Emperor Xuan had forty-two sons: the Empress Liu bore Houzhu; Lady Peng bore the Prince of Shixing, Shuling; Lady Cao bore the Prince of Yuzhang, Shuying; Lady He bore the Prince of Changsha, Shujian, and the Prince of Yidu, Shuming; Lady Wei bore the Prince of Jian'an, Shuqing; Lady Qian bore the Prince of Hedong, Shuxian; Lady Liu bore the Prince of Xincai, Shuqi; Lady Yuan bore the Prince of Jinxi, Shuwen, the Prince of Yiyang, Shuda, and the Prince of Xinhui, Shutan; a Wang consort bore the Prince of Huainan, Shubiao, and the Prince of Bashan, Shuxiong; a Wu consort bore the Prince of Shixing, Shuzhong; Lady Xu bore the Prince of Xunyang, Shuyan; Lady Chunyu bore the Prince of Yueyang, Shushen; Lady Wang bore the Prince of Wuchang, Shuyu; Lady Wei bore the Prince of Xiangdong, Shuping; Lady Shi bore the Prince of Linhe, Shuao, and the Prince of Yuanling, Shuxing; Lady Zeng bore the Prince of Yangshan, Shuxuan; Lady Yang bore the Prince of Xiyang, Shumu; Lady Shen bore the Prince of Nan'an, Shujian, the Prince of Nanjun, Shucheng, the Prince of Yueshan, Shushao, and the Prince of Taiyuan, Shukuang; Lady Yuan bore the Prince of Xinxing, Shuchun; a Wu consort bore the Prince of Badong, Shumo; Lady Liu bore the Prince of Linjiang, Shuxian; Lady Qin bore the Prince of Xinning, Shulong, and the Prince of Xinchang, Shurong.
s0125.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan had forty-two sons: Empress Liu bore Houzhu; Lady Peng bore Prince Shuling of Shixing; Lady Cao bore Prince Shuying of Yuzhang; Lady He bore Prince Shujian of Changsha and Prince Shuming of Yidu; Lady Wei bore Prince Shuqing of Jian'an; Lady Qian bore Prince Shuqi of Xincai; Lady Yuan bore Prince Shuwen of Jinxi, Prince Shuda of Yiyang, and Prince Shutan of Xinhui; a Wang consort bore Prince Shubiao of Huainan and Prince Shuxiong of Bashan; a Wu consort bore Prince Shuzhong of Shixing; Lady Xu bore Prince Shuyan of Xunyang; Lady Chunyu bore Prince Shushen of Yueyang; Lady Wang bore Prince Shuyu of Wuchang; Lady Wei bore Prince Shuping of Xiangdong; Lady Shi bore Prince Shuao of Linhe and Prince Shuxing of Yuanling; Lady Zeng bore Prince Shuxuan of Yangshan; Lady Yang bore Prince Shumu of Xiyang; Lady Shen bore Prince Shujian of Nan'an, Prince Shucheng of Nanjun, Prince Shushao of Yueshan, and Prince Shukuang of Taiyuan; Lady Yuan bore Prince Shuchun of Xinxing; a Wu consort bore Prince Shumo of Badong; Lady Liu bore Prince Shuxian of Linjiang; Lady Qin bore Prince Shulong of Xinning and Prince Shurong of Xinchang.

s0126.literal: The imperial sons Shurui, Shuzhong, Shu
s0126.idiomatic: The imperial sons Shurui, Shuzhong, Shu

s0128.literal: Hong, Shuyi, Shuxun, Shuwu, Shuchu, and Shufeng—eight men in all—had not yet been enfeoffed when the book was compiled.
s0128.idiomatic: Hong, Shuyi, Shuxun, Shuwu, Shuchu, and Shufeng—eight in all—had not yet been enfeoffed when the book was compiled.

s0129.literal: Shuling's rebellion is treated in a separate biography.
s0129.idiomatic: Shuling's rebellion is treated in a separate biography.

s0130.literal: Three sons died young; the original book gives no names.
s0130.idiomatic: Three sons died young; the original book gives no names.

s0131.literal: The eldest son Hong, in the first year of Zhide, was appointed heir of the state of Yuzhang.
s0131.idiomatic: The eldest son Hong, in Zhide year 1, was appointed heir of the state of Yuzhang.

s0132.literal: The Prince of Changsha, Shujian, styled Zicheng, was Emperor Xuan's fourth son.
s0132.idiomatic: Prince Shujian of Changsha, styled Zicheng, was Emperor Xuan's fourth son.

s0133.literal: His mother had originally been a wine-house servant girl in Wu; when Emperor Xuan was still obscure he once went to drink and consorted with her; when he rose high he summoned and appointed her Lady of Graceful Conduct.
s0133.idiomatic: His mother had been a wine-house servant in Wu; when Emperor Xuan was still obscure he once went drinking and took her; when he rose high he made her Lady of Graceful Conduct.

s0134.literal: Shujian in youth was sharp and cunning, fierce and cruel, fond of wine, and especially loved numerology, divination, and talismanic prohibitions; smelting gold and carving jade—he pursued their subtleties to the end.
s0134.idiomatic: Shujian in youth was sharp and cruel, fond of wine, and especially loved numerology, divination, and talismanic arts; smelting gold and carving jade—he pursued their subtleties to the end.

s0135.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng.
s0135.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng.

s0136.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Changsha and at the same time made Eastern Central Commander-in-Chief and Administrator of Wu commandery.
s0136.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 he was made Prince of Changsha and at the same time eastern central commander-in-chief and administrator of Wu commandery.

s0137.literal: In the fourth year he was made Pacifying-Assault General and Inspector of Jiangzhou, with staff clerks appointed.
s0137.idiomatic: In year 4 he was made pacifying-assault general and inspector of Jiangzhou, with staff clerks appointed.

s0138.literal: In the seventh year he was advanced to Cloud-Banner General and Inspector of Yingzhou; before he took up the post he was transferred to Pacifying-Yue Central Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Guangzhou.
s0138.idiomatic: In year 7 he was advanced to cloud-banner general and inspector of Yingzhou; before taking up the post he was transferred to pacifying-yue central commander-in-chief and inspector of Guangzhou.

s0139.literal: Soon he was made Pacifying-North General and Inspector of Hezhou.
s0139.idiomatic: Soon he was made pacifying-north general and inspector of Hezhou.

s0140.literal: In the eighth year he was again made Pacifying-West General and Inspector of Yingzhou.
s0140.idiomatic: In year 8 he was again made pacifying-west general and inspector of Yingzhou.

s0141.literal: In the eleventh year he entered court as Left Assistant General and Governor of Danyang.
s0141.idiomatic: In year 11 he entered court as left assistant general and governor of Danyang.

s0143.literal: At first Shujian and the Prince of Shixing, Shuling, each gathered guests and vied for favor and power, deeply resenting one another.
s0143.idiomatic: At first Shujian and Prince Shuling of Shixing each gathered clients and vied for favor, deeply resenting one another.

s0144.literal: Whenever at court assemblies the guard of honor would not yield precedence, they had to take separate roads and rush forward; attendants at times fought over the road, and there were even deaths.
s0144.idiomatic: At court assemblies neither would yield precedence in the guard of honor; they took separate roads and rushed ahead, and attendants sometimes fought over the road—even to the death.

s0145.literal: When Emperor Xuan fell gravely ill, Shujian, Shuling, and the rest all attended Houzhu in nursing him.
s0145.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan fell gravely ill, Shujian, Shuling, and the rest all attended Houzhu at his bedside.

s0146.literal: Shuling harbored secret designs; he then ordered the pharmacy clerk, saying, "The medicine knife is very dull; it should be sharpened."
s0146.idiomatic: Shuling harbored secret designs and ordered the pharmacy clerk, "The medicine knife is very dull; sharpen it."

s0147.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, in the haste of the moment he again ordered his attendants to fetch a sword from outside; the attendants did not understand and brought the wooden sword worn with court dress, and Shuling was enraged.
s0147.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died, in the haste of the moment he again ordered attendants to fetch a sword from outside; they did not understand and brought the wooden court sword, and Shuling was enraged.

s0148.literal: Shujian, hearing this at his side, suspected trouble and watched what he would do.
s0148.idiomatic: Shujian, hearing this beside him, suspected trouble and watched what he would do.

s0149.literal: On the morrow, at the lesser encoffinment, Shuling hid a sharpened medicine knife in his sleeve, rushed forward, and hacked at Houzhu, striking the nape; Houzhu fainted to the ground. The Empress Dowager and Houzhu's wet-nurse, Lady Wu of Le'an, both used their bodies to shield him, and he escaped harm.
s0149.idiomatic: The next day, at the lesser encoffinment, Shuling hid a sharpened medicine knife in his sleeve, rushed forward, and hacked at Houzhu, striking the nape; Houzhu fainted to the ground. The empress dowager and Houzhu's wet-nurse, Lady Wu of Le'an, both shielded him with their bodies, and he escaped harm.

s0150.literal: Shujian from behind seized Shuling and captured him, also wresting away his knife; he was about to kill him and asked Houzhu, "Shall I finish him now, or wait?"
s0150.idiomatic: Shujian seized Shuling from behind and captured him, wresting away his knife; he was about to kill him and asked Houzhu, "Shall I finish him now, or wait?"

s0152.literal: Shuling had long been very strong; in a moment he broke free by his own exertion, went out through the Cloud-Dragon Gate into the Eastern Palace city, summoned his attendants to cut the Qingxi Bridge road, and released prisoners from the eastern city to serve as fighting men.
s0152.idiomatic: Shuling had long been very strong; in a moment he broke free, went out through the Cloud-Dragon Gate into the eastern palace city, summoned attendants to cut the Qingxi Bridge road, and released eastern-city prisoners to serve as fighting men.

s0153.literal: He also sent men to Xinlin to recall the troops of his command, then himself donned armor, put on a white cloth cap, and climbed the western city gate to recruit the common people.
s0153.idiomatic: He also sent men to Xinlin to recall his command's troops, then donned armor, put on a white cloth cap, and climbed the western city gate to recruit commoners.

s0154.literal: At that time the mass of armies were all defending along the river; within the palace it was empty. Shujian then reported to the Empress Dowager, ordering Crown Prince Household Attendant Sima Shen, on Houzhu's command, to summon Xiao Mohe and order him to attack.
s0154.idiomatic: At that time the armies were all defending along the river; the palace stood empty. Shujian reported to the empress dowager, ordering crown prince household attendant Sima Shen, on Houzhu's command, to summon Xiao Mohe and order him to attack.

s0155.literal: That very day he captured Shuling's generals Dai
s0155.idiomatic: That very day he captured Shuling's generals Dai

s0157.literal: Wen, Tan Qilong, and others; they were sent to the capital and beheaded below the Masters of Writing, their heads displayed along the eastern wall.
s0157.idiomatic: Wen, Tan Qilong, and others; they were sent to the capital and beheaded below the masters of writing, their heads displayed along the eastern wall.

s0158.literal: Shuling, in panic and confusion, did not know what to do; he then killed all his wives and concubines, led several hundred attendants, and fled toward Xinlin. Mohe pursued and beheaded him in Danyang commandery; the remaining partisans were all captured.
s0158.idiomatic: Shuling, in panic, did not know what to do; he killed all his wives and concubines, led several hundred attendants, and fled toward Xinlin. Mohe pursued and beheaded him in Danyang commandery; the remaining partisans were all captured.

s0159.literal: That year, for his merit he was advanced to Rapid Cavalry General, Grandee Opening the Mansion with Ceremonial Parity to the Three Offices, and Inspector of Yangzhou.
s0159.idiomatic: That year, for his merit he was advanced to rapid cavalry general, grandee opening the mansion with ceremonial parity to the three offices, and inspector of Yangzhou.

s0160.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Works, with his general and inspector posts unchanged.
s0160.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to minister of works, retaining his general and inspector posts.

s0161.literal: At that time Houzhu was wounded and could not attend to affairs; whether great or small, all government was entrusted to Shujian for decision, and so his power dominated the court.
s0161.idiomatic: At that time Houzhu was wounded and could not govern; great and small affairs were all entrusted to Shujian, and his power dominated the court.

s0162.literal: Shujian thereupon gave free rein to arrogance and license, and many of his acts were unlawful; Houzhu therefore grew distant and suspicious of him.
s0162.idiomatic: Shujian thereupon grew arrogant and lawless; Houzhu therefore grew distant and suspicious of him.

s0163.literal: Kong Fan, Guan Bin, Shi Wenqing, and the like—all old eastern-palace ministers—day and night secretly gathered his faults.
s0163.idiomatic: Kong Fan, Guan Bin, Shi Wenqing, and the like—all old eastern-palace ministers—day and night secretly gathered his faults.

s0164.literal: In the first year of Zhide an edict ordered him to use the ceremonial of the Three Offices under his present title and go out as Inspector of Jiangzhou.
s0164.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 an edict ordered him to use three-office ceremonial under his present title and go out as inspector of Jiangzhou.

s0165.literal: Before he departed, there was soon another edict making him again Rapid Cavalry General and again Minister of Works—in truth intending to strip away his power.
s0165.idiomatic: Before he departed, another edict soon made him again rapid cavalry general and again minister of works—in truth intending to strip away his power.

s0166.literal: Shujian was ill at ease and gradually resentful; he then practiced left-hand ways and malign sorcery to seek blessing, carving wooden puppets, clothing them in Taoist dress, fitting them with mechanisms so they could bow and kneel, offering sacrifices to them day and night under the sun and moon, with curses and imprecations pronounced over them.
s0166.idiomatic: Shujian grew uneasy and resentful; he then practiced left-hand sorcery to seek blessing, carving wooden puppets, clothing them in Taoist dress, fitting them with mechanisms so they could bow and kneel, offering sacrifices day and night under sun and moon with curses pronounced over them.

s0167.literal: That winter someone submitted a memorial reporting the affair; investigation proved it all true, and Houzhu summoned Shujian and imprisoned him in the Western Quarters, intending to kill him.
s0167.idiomatic: That winter someone memorialized reporting the affair; investigation proved it true, and Houzhu summoned Shujian and imprisoned him in the western quarters, intending to kill him.

s0168.literal: That night he ordered a close attendant to proclaim the edict and enumerate his crimes. Shujian replied, "Your servant's original intent held no other purpose—I only sought to win intimate favor. Your servant has violated Heaven's law and deserves death ten thousand times over; on the day I die I shall surely see Shuling. I beg that the bright edict be proclaimed to reproach him in the realm below the Nine Springs."
s0168.idiomatic: That night he ordered a close attendant to proclaim the edict and enumerate his crimes. Shujian replied, "My original intent held no other purpose—I only sought to win intimate favor. I have violated Heaven's law and deserve death ten thousand times over; on the day I die I shall surely see Shuling. I beg that the bright edict be proclaimed to reproach him in the realm below."

s0169.literal: Houzhu, moved by his former merit, then pardoned him, specially removing him from office and sending him back to his princely residence.
s0169.idiomatic: Houzhu, moved by his former merit, pardoned him, specially removing him from office and sending him back to his residence.

s0170.literal: Soon he was reappointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Suppressing General.
s0170.idiomatic: Soon he was reappointed attendant-in-ordinary and left suppressing general.

s0171.literal: In the second year he was again given drum-and-pipe music and an oil-canopy carriage.
s0171.idiomatic: In year 2 he was again given drum-and-pipe music and an oil-canopy carriage.

s0172.literal: In the third year he went out as Campaigning-West General and Inspector of Jingzhou.
s0172.idiomatic: In year 3 he went out as campaigning-west general and inspector of Jingzhou.

s0173.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced to Central Army Grand General and Grandee Opening the Mansion with Ceremonial Parity to the Three Offices.
s0173.idiomatic: In year 4 he was advanced to central army grand general and grandee opening the mansion with ceremonial parity to the three offices.

s0174.literal: In the second year of Zhenming his term expired and he returned to the capital.
s0174.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 2 his term expired and he returned to the capital.

s0175.literal: In the third year he entered the Pass and was moved to Guazhou; his name was changed to Shuxian.
s0175.idiomatic: In year 3 he entered the Pass and was moved to Guazhou; his name was changed to Shuxian.

s0176.literal: Shuxian had always been noble and did not know how a household makes its living; by then he and his consort, Lady Shen, sold wine and took in lodgers for hire.
s0176.idiomatic: Shuxian had always been noble and did not know how a household makes its living; by then he and his consort, Lady Shen, sold wine and took in lodgers for hire.

s0177.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was made Administrator of Suining commandery.
s0177.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was administrator of Suining commandery.

s0178.literal: The Prince of Jian'an, Shuqing, styled Zibi, was Emperor Xuan's fifth son.
s0178.idiomatic: Prince Shuqing of Jian'an, styled Zibi, was Emperor Xuan's fifth son.

s0179.literal: By nature he was upright and had talent and capacity; his appearance was very imposing.
s0179.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and capable; his appearance was very imposing.

s0180.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Jian'an and appointed Eastern Central Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Dongyang.
s0180.idiomatic: In Taijian year 4 he was made Prince of Jian'an and appointed eastern central commander-in-chief and inspector of Dongyang.

s0181.literal: In the seventh year he was made Cloud-Banner General and Inspector of Yingzhou, with staff clerks appointed.
s0181.idiomatic: In year 7 he was made cloud-banner general and inspector of Yingzhou, with staff clerks appointed.

s0182.literal: In the ninth year he was advanced to Pacifying-South General and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
s0182.idiomatic: In year 9 he was advanced to pacifying-south general and inspector of Xiangzhou.

s0183.literal: When Houzhu succeeded to the throne he was advanced to Pacifying-South General.
s0183.idiomatic: When Houzhu succeeded to the throne he was advanced to pacifying-south general.

s0184.literal: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Suppressing-Right General, and Director of the Palace Secretariat.
s0184.idiomatic: He was again made attendant-in-ordinary, suppressing-right general, and director of the palace secretariat.

s0185.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.
s0185.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervisor of the palace secretariat.

s0186.literal: He was transferred to director of the Secretariat.
s0186.idiomatic: He was made director of the Secretariat.

s0187.literal: The Prince of Yidu, Shuming, styled Zizhao, was Emperor Xuan's sixth son.
s0187.idiomatic: Prince Shuming of Yidu, styled Zizhao, was Emperor Xuan's sixth son.

s0188.literal: His bearing was beautifully handsome; his manner gentle and weak, in appearance like a woman.
s0188.idiomatic: His bearing was beautifully handsome; his manner gentle and weak, in appearance like a woman.

s0189.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Yidu and soon appointed Pacifying-Assault General, with staff clerks appointed.
s0189.idiomatic: In Taijian year 5 he was made Prince of Yidu and soon appointed pacifying-assault general, with staff clerks appointed.

s0190.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Eastern Central Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Dongyang; soon he was made Light-Carriage General and Commandant of the Guards.
s0190.idiomatic: In year 7 he was appointed eastern central commander-in-chief and inspector of Dongyang; soon he was made light-carriage general and commandant of the guards.

s0191.literal: In the thirteenth year he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Cloud-Banner General, and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
s0191.idiomatic: In year 13 he went out as bearer of the staff, cloud-banner general, and inspector of South Xuzhou.

s0192.literal: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Assistant General.
s0192.idiomatic: He was again made attendant-in-ordinary and right assistant general.

s0193.literal: In the fourth year of Zhide he was advanced to Pacifying-Right General.
s0193.idiomatic: In Zhide year 4 he was advanced to pacifying-right general.

s0194.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the Pass; in the Daye era of Sui he was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
s0194.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the Pass; under Sui's Daye era he was vice director of the court of the imperial clan.

s0195.literal: The Prince of Hedong, Shuxian, styled Zigong, was Emperor Xuan's ninth son.
s0195.idiomatic: Prince Shuxian of Hedong, styled Zigong, was Emperor Xuan's ninth son.

s0196.literal: By nature he was respectful and cautious, clever and fond of learning.
s0196.idiomatic: By nature he was respectful and cautious, clever and fond of learning.

s0197.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Hedong.
s0197.idiomatic: In Taijian year 5 he was made Prince of Hedong.

s0198.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Pacifying-Assault General, with staff clerks appointed.
s0198.idiomatic: In year 7 he was appointed pacifying-assault general, with staff clerks appointed.

s0199.literal: Soon he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Military Adviser General, and Commander-in-Chief of South Xuzhou Military Affairs and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
s0199.idiomatic: Soon he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, military adviser general, and commander-in-chief of South Xuzhou military affairs and inspector of South Xuzhou.

s0200.literal: In the twelfth year he died, aged thirteen.
s0200.idiomatic: In year 12 he died, aged thirteen.
